key_insight: AEAPTMS amino-silane passivation makes mixed-halide perovskite surfaces electronically more uniform, increasing and stabilizing the surface photovoltage while reducing grain-boundary barriers.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical route to lower photovoltage losses and improve carrier-landscape stability in perovskite solar cells through nanoscale surface passivation.
method: Measured dark contact potential difference (CPD) and illuminated surface photovoltage (SPV)
Compared grain-boundary vs grain-interior potential dynamics and wavelength-dependent SPV
evidence_signal: Passivated films showed CPD distribution narrowing from ~45.7 to ~14.6 mV, SPV rising from ~345 to ~417 mV, and stabilization time constant dropping from ~840 to ~470 s.
watch_item: The results are based on thin-film nanoscale measurements, so device-level performance gains and long-term operational stability still need direct validation.
paper_title: Understanding surface potential dynamics of passivated perovskites via Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
